We are dedicated to fostering diverse musical practices that enrich lives and the human experience. By promoting ethical and innovative career paths in performance, teaching, and the music industry, we empower you to achieve your highest artistic, scholarly, and professional potential. The Department of Music offers a robust polytechnic education grounded in both academic and performance-based study. Students pursue either a Bachelor of Arts or a Bachelor of Music, selecting from options such as Music Industry Studies, Performance, Composition, Music Education, or a general liberal arts pathway. Faculty combine active professional careers with teaching, bringing a contemporary and global perspective to music education. Courses engage students with music theory, history, production, and pedagogy, while promoting artistic growth and critical thinking. All students participate in ensembles and receive individual instrumental instruction to build foundational and specialized expertise. The department fosters a dynamic performance culture with over 20 ensembles ranging from traditional symphonic groups to Mariachi and commercial music. Students showcase their work in concerts, recordings, and festivals, while learning in fully equipped studios and production labs. courses.title: Introduction to Music
courses.description: [GE 3A] Introduction to the concepts of reading and writing music; cross-cultural study of music, its values, structures, and functions.

courses.title: Music Appreciation
courses.description: [GE 3A] An understanding of the elements of music and various musical forms and stylistic periods. Actively and perceptively listen to a wide variety of music.

courses.title: World of Music
courses.description: [GE 3A] Introduction to selected music cultures of the world. At least one music culture from each continent will be covered.

courses.title: Careers in Music
courses.description: Survey of careers in music and related fields, with emphasis on entrepreneurship and individual career options and planning. Overview of the roles and responsibilities in music performance, education, composition, production, and business.

courses.title: Music Foundations
courses.description: Musicianship basics for the music major. A hands-on course in developing rudimentary musicianship skills and relating them to music notation where appropriate. May be tested out of by advanced musicians.
courses.repeat_for_credit: May be taken multiple times Minimum - Maximum Units: Total credit limited to 6 units applicable to a degree.

courses.title: Introduction to Music Technology
courses.description: Introduction to the essential elements and application of computer-based music technology. Principles, uses, and techniques for working with MIDI, notation, and sequencing software and hardware.

courses.title: History of American Popular Music
courses.description: Survey of popular music history in the United States, from minstrel songs and Tin Pan Alley to the emergence of rock ‘n’ roll and to the most current popular music genres.

courses.title: Jazz and Beyond
courses.description: [GE 3A] A survey of jazz and jazz-related music from America and around the world.

courses.title: Beginning Piano I
courses.description: Beginning class piano instruction. Reading and playing simple compositions. No previous experience required. May be taken up to two times for a total credit of 2 units.

courses.title: Class Piano I
courses.description: Beginning class piano instruction. Development of ability to play simple solo and duet compositions and chords in all keys. Chord progressions and harmonization of melodies using primary chords. Transposition. Technical studies and scales.

courses.title: Class Piano II
courses.description: Continuing class piano instruction. Simple solo and duet compositions and chords in all keys. Chord progressions and harmonization of melodies using primary and secondary chords. Transposition, modulation, simple improvisation. Technical studies and all major and minor scales.
courses.prerequisites: Music majors only; and MU 112A or MU 1121A or equivalent knowledge via instructor approval.

courses.title: Jazz Improvisation, Beginning
courses.description: Beginning experience in jazz improvisational techniques. Chords, key, scales, melodic and rhythmic application, stylistic devices and procedures necessary to the development of spontaneous and creative soloistic invention. May be taken up to two times for a total credit of 2 units.

courses.title: Introduction to Music Theory
courses.description: Reading, playing, singing, listening to and analyzing: rhythms, simple and compound meters, dotted notes; the pitches of the clefs, major and minor scales and key signatures, altered minor scales, triads, triads in major and minor keys and their inversions, minor key signatures, major and minor key relationships. Corequisite(s): MU 2211A .
courses.prerequisites: Placement according to department entrance/placement exam.

courses.title: Music Theory II: Chromatic Harmony
courses.description: Second-level subdivision of the beat, syncopation; Secondary dominant and leading-tone chords and inversions, modulation, part-writing, harmonic analysis, non-chord tones, larger tertian structures, borrowed tones and chords.

courses.title: Songwriting
courses.description: Introductory study of the thematic, poetic, melodic, structural, rhythmic and harmonic components of a song. Individual projects in songwriting.
courses.repeat_for_credit: May be taken multiple times Minimum - Maximum Units: Total credit limited to 9 units applicable to a degree, with a maximum of 3 units per semester.

courses.title: Brass Class
courses.description: Beginning and intermediate instruction in the fundamentals of playing brass instruments. No previous experience required. May be taken up to two times for a total credit of 2 units.

courses.title: Guitar Class
courses.description: Beginning and intermediate instruction in the fundamentals of playing guitar. Development of right and left hand finger coordination, strumming and finger-picking techniques; note and chord reading skills. No previous experience required. May be taken up to two times for a total credit of 2 units.

courses.title: Percussion Class
courses.description: Beginning and intermediate instruction on percussion instruments. Stick and mallet technique including membrane, metal, non-pitched and pitched instruments. No previous experience required. May be taken up to two times for a total credit of 2 units.

courses.title: Beginning Strings
courses.description: Beginning instruction on the violin, viola, cello, or bass. Development of bow and finger coordination, tone production and note reading skills. No previous experience required. May be taken up to two times for a total credit of 2 units.

courses.title: Voice Class
courses.description: Beginning and intermediate instruction in singing. Foundations of technique with emphasis on posture, breath management, tone production, diction, and communication. Song performances with feedback provided to practice for improvement. May be taken up to two times for a total credit of 2 units.

courses.title: Woodwind Class
courses.description: Beginning and intermediate instruction on the flute, clarinet, oboe, bassoon, or saxophone. No previous experience required. May be taken up to two times for a total credit of 2 units.

courses.title: World Music Class
courses.description: Beginning and intermediate instruction on instruments from world music traditions. No previous experience required. May be taken up to two times for a total credit of 2 units.

courses.title: Electronic Music Composition and Production
courses.description: Survey of techniques and skills used in electronic music composition and production. Advanced study of audio synthesis, sampling, virtual instruments and sample libraries, creative uses of audio processing, and related topics. Study of representative works in both popular and experimental genres.

courses.title: Beginning Piano II
courses.description: Continuing class piano instruction. Continued development of reading and playing skills at the keyboard. Some previous experience required. May be taken up to two times for a total credit of 2 units.
courses.prerequisites: Sophomore standing and instructor consent. Any candidate for this course must have demonstrated the ability to work individually and be able to gain considerably in this way.

courses.title: Class Piano III
courses.description: Second year of class piano instruction for music majors. Continued development of music reading and performance skills, covering compositions of many styles. Transposition, harmonization in various keyboard styles, improvisation, ensemble and accompaniment study. Technical studies and all major/ minor scales.
courses.prerequisites: Music majors only; and MU 113A, MU 1131A or equivalent.

courses.title: Class Piano IV
courses.description: Final semester of class piano instruction for music majors. Continued development of music reading and performance skills, covering compositions of many styles. Transposition, harmonization in various keyboard styles, improvisation, ensemble and accompaniment skills. Proficiency in all scales and arpeggios, sight-reading.
courses.prerequisites: Music majors only; and MU 212A, MU 2121A or equivalent.

courses.title: Form and Analysis
courses.description: Study and experience in solving problems related to analyzing musical forms. Song and dance, sonata, rondo, concerto, and variation. Application of strategies for detailed listening to these musics.

courses.title: Music Theory: Classical I
courses.description: Materials and methods of composition and analysis for Western classical music, focusing mainly on diatonic materials. Scale realizations, cadences, related-key modulations, the Rule of the Octave, typical patterns (schemata), and four-part writing. Study of forms, including sentence, period, small binary, and small ternary (rounded binary). The student must be enrolled in musicianship concurrently with all theory classes unless they have completed all musicianship courses for their degree program.

courses.title: Jazz and Pop Harmony and Techniques
courses.description: The study of the harmonic and rhythmic idioms used in popular music and jazz. Covers the aural and written language of chord symbols, analysis and practical use of typical pop and jazz chord progressions and harmonies, the writing of lead sheets, using a “rhythm section,” and an introduction to commercial and jazz arranging techniques. The student must be enrolled in musicianship concurrently with all theory classes unless they have completed all musicianship courses for their degree program.

courses.title: 20th and 21st Century Music Theory
courses.description: Survey of music theory approaches to Western music from the 20th century to the present. Study of representative works in various styles and genres, including a variety of relevant analytical and compositional techniques. The student must be enrolled in musicianship concurrently with all theory classes unless they have completed all musicianship courses for their degree program.

courses.title: Musicianship I
courses.description: Drill and practice of sight-reading skills and rhythmic and melodic dictation, including software-assisted tutoring. Should be taken during the same semester as MU 1201. Corequisite(s): MU 1201 .
courses.prerequisites: Placement according to department entrance/placement exam.

courses.title: Musicianship II
courses.description: Drill and practice of sight-reading skills and rhythmic, melodic, and harmonic dictation including software-assisted tutoring.

courses.title: Composition
courses.description: Beginning exercises in basic techniques of composition, with an emphasis on analyzing and synthesizing the styles of the great composers of art music.
courses.repeat_for_credit: May be taken multiple times Minimum - Maximum Units: Total credit limited to 6 units applicable to a degree, with a maximum of 3 units per semester.

courses.title: The Digital Audio Workstation
courses.description: Overview of the applied use of digital audio workstations (DAWs) for music production. Lecture and hands-on projects in recording, sequencing, editing, signal processing, and mixing in a DAW. Exploration of industry-standard DAWs such as Pro Tools and Logic Pro. Lectures and projects in digital audio fundamentals, importing and exporting media, file formats, storage, playback, and delivery.

courses.title: Songwriting II
courses.description: Further study of the thematic, poetic, melodic, structural, rhythmic and harmonic components of a song. Individual projects in songwriting.

courses.title: Intermediate Guitar Class
courses.description: Intermediate instruction in playing the guitar. Development of right- and left-hand finger coordination, strumming and finger-picking techniques; note- and chord-reading skills. May be taken up to two times for a total credit of 2 units.

courses.title: Intermediate Strings
courses.description: Intermediate instruction on the violin, viola, cello, or bass. Further development of technique: all scales, shifting, vibrato, and advanced bowings. May be taken up to two times for a total credit of 2 units.
courses.prerequisites: Instructor consent; Successful completion of Beginning Strings or equivalent; Student should have basic note reading skills and a foundation on the instrument and Students may be placed in this class at the discretion of the instructor.

courses.title: Introduction to Music Education
courses.description: Exploration of music learning research and music education philosophies and methods in American music education. Discovery of current trends in contemporary inclusive music education. Includes 20 hours of field observation.

courses.title: Diction for Singers
courses.description: Study of the International Phonetic Alphabet (IPA), pronunciation of languages needed to perform great song and operatic literature. Activities and exercises in Italian, French, German, and English diction. Translating texts into IPA and performance of songs or arias in these languages. May be taken up to two times for a total credit of 4 units.
courses.prerequisites: Concurrent enrollment in MU 3811 or MU 4610 , or 2 units from the following: MU 1340 , MU 1770 , or MU 1811 .

courses.title: Performance Seminar
courses.description: Weekly seminar/workshop with opportunity to perform for other students and encourage discussion of technique, interpretation, and style. May be taken unlimited times. Corequisite(s): Concurrent enrollment in a studio course.
courses.repeat_for_credit: May be taken multiple times Minimum - Maximum Units: May be repeated up to 10 units.

courses.title: Music Theory III: Advanced Music Theory
courses.description: Further study of chromatic harmony including augmented 6th chords and chromatic modulation; evolution and re-ordering of musical elements in the 20th Century including expanded use of rhythm and meters, free tonality, atonality, bi-tonality, symmetry, multi-layered techniques, ultra-rationalism, minimalist techniques.

courses.title: Tonal Counterpoint
courses.description: Study and experience in analyzing and writing tonal counterpoint. Including modes, canon, species counterpoint, contrapuntal techniques. Vocal polyphony and instrumental inventions and fugues.

courses.title: Beginning Conducting
courses.description: Introduction to the basic elements of conducting, including: non-verbal communication and gesture, hand independence, baton technique, preparatory beats, patterns, cues, releases, fermatas, score study and problem-solving rehearsal skills.
courses.prerequisites: MU 2211A , MU 1131A , and MU 2201 or MU 2202 .

courses.title: Instrumental Conducting
courses.description: Study of and experience in instrumental conducting techniques. Problem-solving and decision-making as it pertains to conducting instrumental ensembles to include: transpositions, score study, rehearsal techniques, programming, aural skills, error detection and gesture as effective non-verbal communication.

courses.title: Choral Conducting
courses.description: Study of and experience in choral conducting techniques. Problem-solving and decision-making as it pertains to conducting vocal ensembles. Practical experience in implementing those decisions.

courses.title: Composing for Film and Television
courses.description: Continued study of computer-based music technology, including the use of virtual instruments and samplers. Practical experience in creating digital music compositions, arrangements, and film and video game scores using a MIDI/Digital Audio Workstation.

courses.title: Instrumentation and Arranging
courses.description: Study of the instruments of the orchestra and symphonic band. Transpositions, notation, scoring, and arranging for instruments and small ensembles.

courses.title: History of Technology in Music
courses.description: [GE 3C, 4C, or 5D] Survey of music technologies, including the musical, cultural, and philosophical forces governing them, from the monochord of Ancient Greece through contemporary life.
courses.prerequisites: Junior or senior standing; and completion of GE Areas 1 and 2, or Areas A and B4 are recommended.

courses.title: Music of Mexico
courses.description: Survey of music and dance of Mexico focusing on folk instruments and music patterns, cultural crossover between Hispanic and indigenous music heritages.

courses.title: Popular Music Production
courses.description: Lecture and project-based exploration of common-practice production techniques in popular music. Investigation into digital audio workstations (DAWs) and other technologies used in beat making, sequencing, sampling, recording, and mixing electronic popular music. Overview of production practices in late-20th century through the present. Focus on predominantly electronic popular music styles including contemporary R&B, hip-hop, electro-pop, electroclash, EDM, house, and technopop.

courses.title: Jazz Improvisation, Advanced
courses.description: Traditional and contemporary techniques of improvisation. Basic and advanced chords, keys, and scales are emphasized through melodic, rhythmic, and harmonic applications. May be taken up to two times for a total credit of 2 units.
courses.repeat_for_credit: May be taken multiple times Minimum - Maximum Units: Total credit limited to 2 units.

courses.title: Women in Music
courses.description: Study of contributions women have made as composers and performers. Student presentation of a culminating study.

courses.title: Ethnomusicology: Theory, History, and Field Methods
courses.description: Introduction to the field of ethnomusicology, including its history, theory, and ethnographic field methods.

courses.title: Music Theory: Classical II
courses.description: Materials and methods of composition and analysis for Western music, focusing mainly on chromatic materials. Typical chromatic patterns (schemata) and enharmonic modulations. Transformation theory. Study of forms, including lied, and sonata forms. Applications to film, television, and video game music.

courses.title: Musicianship III
courses.description: Drill and practice of sight-reading skills and rhythmic, melodic, and harmonic dictation including software-assisted tutoring.

courses.title: Musicianship IV
courses.description: Drill and practice of sight-reading skills and rhythmic, melodic, and harmonic dictation including software-assisted tutoring.

courses.title: Composition II
courses.description: Survey of contemporary techniques in composition, music notation and contemporary literature. Encouragement to develop music in tune with personal style while exploring a variety of compositional techniques.

courses.title: Music Recording
courses.description: Project-based overview of the recording arts. History of recording technology. Introduction to professional recording studio equipment and techniques, including microphones, signal processing, and acoustic principles. Professional techniques for recording, editing, and mixing using Pro Tools-HD systems and other specialized equipment.

courses.title: Piano Pedagogy
courses.description: Introduction to piano pedagogy. Diverse teaching approaches and techniques, with primary focus on beginning and intermediate repertoire. Study and review of existing methods, tools, and technology available to piano teachers. Theoretic and hands-on components. Teaching observations and working with students. May be taken up to two times for a total credit of 4 units.
courses.prerequisites: At least two semesters of MU 1750 , MU 1751 , or MU 1811 .

courses.title: Brass Fundamentals
courses.description: Fundamentals of playing and teaching the trumpet, trombone, horn, tuba for music majors and minors who plan to teach music in the public schools K-12. Development of embouchure, tone, note reading skills; basic brass pedagogy.

courses.title: Percussion Fundamentals
courses.description: Fundamentals of playing and teaching percussion instruments for music majors and minors who plan to teach music in the public schools K-12; stick and mallet technique for membrane, metal, non-pitched and pitched instruments. Basic percussion pedagogy.

courses.title: String Fundamentals
courses.description: Fundamentals of playing and teaching the violin, viola, cello, and string bass for music majors and minors who plan to teach music in the public schools K-12. Development of bow and finger coordination, tone, note reading skills; basic string pedagogy.

courses.title: Vocal Pedagogy
courses.description: Study of the science and physiology of the vocal instrument and exploration of the teaching of singing based on principles of healthy vocal production. Experience applying acquired knowledge through singing assignments. May be taken up to two times for a total credit of 4 units.
courses.repeat_for_credit: May be taken multiple times Minimum - Maximum Units: Total credit limited to 4 units.

courses.title: Woodwind Fundamentals
courses.description: Fundamentals of playing and teaching woodwinds: flute, oboe, clarinet, bassoon, and saxophone for music majors and minors who plan to teach music in the public schools K- 12. Development of embouchure, finger coordination, tone, note reading skills; basic woodwind pedagogy.

courses.title: Guitar Fundamentals
courses.description: Fundamentals of playing and teaching guitar for music majors and minors who plan to teach music in the public schools K-12; right- and left-hand techniques for nylon and steel-string guitar pedagogy.

courses.title: Secondary Choral Methods
courses.description: Study and analysis of problems and solutions involved in developing and operating a vocal music program in K-12 schools. Developing the adolescent voice. Common teaching methods, strategies and assessments. 8 hours field observations/service.

courses.title: Secondary Instrumental Methods
courses.description: Study and analysis of problems and solutions involved in developing and operating an instrumental music program in K-12 schools. Common teaching methods, strategies, and assessments. 8 hours field observation/service.
courses.prerequisites: MU 3321A or MU 332; and MU 3341A or MU 334.
courses.repeat_for_credit: May be taken only once Minimum - Maximum Units: 8 hours field observation/service.

courses.title: Teaching Music Literacy
courses.description: Music methods, texts, songs, recordings, and instruments used in the elementary classroom, and their application to literacy building. Investigation of music literacy activities appropriate for various grade levels, including improvisation and composition. Practical strategies for teaching music notation. Application of music to connect across the curriculum.

courses.title: Brass Ensemble
courses.description: Study and performance of chamber to large brass ensemble literature.

courses.title: Woodwind Ensemble
courses.description: Study and performance of chamber to large woodwind ensemble literature. May be taken unlimited times.

courses.title: Percussion Ensemble
courses.description: Study and performance of chamber to large percussion ensemble literature.

courses.title: String Ensemble
courses.description: Study, rehearsal and performance of string orchestra and chamber ensemble literature from all musical periods by composers from around the world.
courses.prerequisites: Audition; and Minimum 2 years of instrument experience.

courses.title: Collaborative Piano
courses.description: Designed to foster collaborative skills in pianists. Sight-reading, rehearsal and performance of collaborative vocal and instrumental repertoire of many styles. Develops ensemble skills such as balance, rhythm and timing when playing with other musicians. May be taken up to four times for a total credit of 4 units.
courses.repeat_for_credit: May be taken multiple times Minimum - Maximum Units: Total credit limited to 9 units.

courses.title: Cal Poly Pomona Collaborative Piano Ensemble
courses.description: Designed to foster collaborative skills in pianists with performances throughout the semester. Sight-reading, rehearsal and performance of collaborative vocal and instrumental repertoire with piano/pianos, from different eras and styles. Develops ensemble skills such as balance, rhythm and timing when playing with other musicians.
courses.prerequisites: Enrollment by audition. All members must have prior experience on a relevant instrument.
courses.repeat_for_credit: May be taken multiple times Minimum - Maximum Units: Total credit limited to 8 units, with a maximum of 1 unit per semester.

courses.title: Guitar Ensemble
courses.description: Study and performance of guitar ensemble literature. May be taken unlimited times.

courses.title: World Music Ensemble
courses.description: Study and performance of Soul ensemble literature.

courses.title: Black Music Ensemble
courses.description: The study, rehearsal, and presentation of classic and contemporary Black American vocal and instrumental repertoire, presented via culturally specific performance practices for the campus and extended community.
courses.prerequisites: Enrollment by audition. Must have prior experience on a relevant instrument.
courses.repeat_for_credit: May be taken multiple times Minimum - Maximum Units: Total credit limited to 9 units, with a maximum of 1 unit per semester.

courses.title: Piano Ensemble
courses.description: Designed to foster collaborative skills in pianists. Sight-reading, rehearsal and performance of piano ensemble repertoire from different eras and styles. Ensembles can include piano four-hands, two-piano, and groups of 3-4 keyboard players on multiple instruments.

courses.title: Cal Poly Pomona Piano Ensemble
courses.description: Designed to foster collaborative skills in pianists with performances throughout the semester. Sight-reading, rehearsal and performance of piano ensemble repertoire from different eras and styles. Ensembles can include piano four-hands, two-piano, and groups of 3-10 keyboard players on multiple instruments. Develops ensemble skills such as balance, rhythm and timing when playing with other musicians.
courses.prerequisites: Enrollment by audition. All members must have prior piano playing experience.
courses.repeat_for_credit: May be taken multiple times Minimum - Maximum Units: Total credit limited to 8 units, with a maximum of 1 unit per semester.

courses.title: Orchestra
courses.description: Rehearsal and performance of orchestral literature from all musical periods, styles and genres by composers from around the world. Students from all majors with prior experience on an orchestral instrument may audition and enroll.
courses.prerequisites: Audition and prior training on an orchestral instrument.

courses.title: Symphonic Winds
courses.description: This ensemble performs repertory of both traditional and contemporary compositional styles. Comprised of 50-60 select music majors, minors and talented non-music majors who qualify through audition, ensemble members will develop a deeper sensitivity toward outstanding musicianship, historical style, performance practices, and aesthetics. In addition, high expectations on individual responsibility to learn his/her part will be required at each rehearsal. An audition and a year-long commitment are required for enrollment.
courses.prerequisites: Enrollment by Audition, prior experience on a wind or percussion instrument, and audition for seat placement.

courses.title: Wind Ensemble
courses.description: The CPP Wind Ensemble represents the finest woodwind, brass and percussion students at Cal Poly Pomona and exclusively performs wind band literature deemed of the highest quality from the repertory of both traditional and contemporary compositional styles. Comprised of 50 select music majors, minors, and talented non-music majors who qualify through audition, ensemble members will develop a deeper sensitivity toward outstanding musicianship, historical style, performance practices, and aesthetics. In addition, high expectations on individual responsibility to learn his/her part will be required at each rehearsal. An audition and a year-long commitment are required for enrollment. Development of outstanding musicianship, performance practices, and aesthetics.
courses.prerequisites: Enrollment by Audition, prior experience on a wind or percussion instrument, and audition for seat placement.

courses.title: Jazz Band
courses.description: Rehearsal and performance of jazz ensemble and jazz ensemble related music. May be taken unlimited times.

courses.title: Concert Band
courses.description: The CPP Concert Band is open to all majors, minors and campus community members interested in performing traditional and contemporary concert band literature. Although an audition is not required for enrollment, a non-stress audition will be conducted for appropriate seating placement and part assignment. Previous experience performing on a wind or percussion instrument is required for enrollment.
courses.prerequisites: Enrollment by audition. All members must have prior experience on a wind or percussion instrument and audition for seat placement.

courses.title: Jazz Combo
courses.description: Rehearsal and performance of small group jazz and jazz related music.

courses.title: New Music Ensemble
courses.description: Chamber ensemble focusing on repertoire for small and large combinations of instruments with special attention paid towards the workshop and performance of newly composed student and faculty works. May be taken unlimited times.

courses.title: Latin American Ensemble
courses.description: Study and performance of Latin American ensemble literature.

courses.title: Mariachi
courses.description: Rehearsal and performance of traditional and contemporary Mariachi repertoire, style, and technique, for the campus and extended communities.
courses.prerequisites: Enrollment by audition. All members must have prior experience on a relevant instrument.

courses.title: Electronic Music Ensemble
courses.description: Rehearsal and performance of MIDI and electronic works of a variety of genres from around the world. May be taken unlimited times.
courses.prerequisites: Audition; and prior training a related band string, keyboard or voice instrument.

courses.title: Concert Choir
courses.description: Rehearsal and performance of choral literature for mixed voices, from all musical periods by composers from around the world. This course is limited to students who have had vocal and/or choral experience in high school or college and who show proficiency for reading and understanding choral literature. This course is limited to students who have had vocal and/or choral experience in high school or college and who show proficiency for reading and understanding choral literature.

courses.title: Music Theatre Workshop
courses.description: Rehearsal and preparation for performance of operatic, operetta, and musical theatre literature. Students enrolled in MU 3621L are required to enroll in MU 3631L for semesters in which one production is in rehearsal/performance over a two-semester period. MU 3631L and MU 3621L are a sequence requiring a one year commitment from the student.

courses.title: Music Theatre Production
courses.description: Rehearsal and performance of a complete opera, operetta, or musical theatre or performance of selections from these genres. Technical crews, singing, and acting. Students enrolled in MU 3631L are required to enroll in MU 3621L for semesters in which one production is in rehearsal/performance over a two-semester period. MU 3621L and MU 3631L are a sequence requiring a one year commitment from the student.
courses.prerequisites: Audition, and singing and acting proficiency.

courses.title: Chamber Singers
courses.description: Rehearsal and performance of choral literature for small choral ensembles, from all musical periods by composers from around the world.
courses.prerequisites: Audition; and required proficiencies determined by audition.

courses.title: African American Vocal Ensemble
courses.description: Rehearsal and performance of jazz and jazz related vocal ensemble music.

courses.title: Interpretation for Singers
courses.description: A performance workshop based on individual student participation in which communication through the singing voice and the special problems of the singer/actor are explored in depth. Improvisation, acting, communication. May be taken up to two times for a total credit of 4 units.
courses.prerequisites: MU 1340 , MU 1770 , or MU 1811 ; Solo performance experience; and non Music majors must audition.
courses.repeat_for_credit: May be taken multiple times Minimum - Maximum Units: Repeatable up to 4 units.

courses.title: Songwriter Showcase
courses.description: Rehearsal and performance of song literature and original songwriting.

courses.title: Studio Strings
courses.description: Weekly individual instructional lessons. Repertoire and technical studies at a higher level than MU 171, MU 1710, or MU 1711, selected appropriately for violin, viola, cello, or double bass. Jury examination required. Available to Music majors only. May be taken up to five times for a total credit of 5 units. Corequisite(s): MU 2700 and appropriate ensemble.
courses.prerequisites: MU 1710 , MU 1711 , or MU 1811 ; appropriate ensemble; passing entrance requirements for upper division studio; and instructor consent.

courses.title: Studio Brass
courses.description: Weekly individual instructional lessons. Repertoire and technical studies at a higher level than MU 172, MU 1720, or MU 1721, selected appropriately for trumpet, horn, trombone, tuba, or euphonium. Jury examination required. Available to Music majors only. May be taken up to five times for a total credit of 5 units. Available to Music majors only. Corequisite(s): MU 2700 .
courses.prerequisites: MU 1720 , MU 1721 , or MU 1811 ; appropriate ensemble; passing entrance requirements for upper division studio; and instructor consent.

courses.title: Studio Woodwind
courses.description: Weekly individual instructional lessons. Repertoire and technical studies at a higher level than MU 1730, or MU 1731, selected appropriately for flute, oboe, clarinet, bassoon, or saxophone. Jury examination required. Available to Music majors only. May be taken up to five times for a total credit of 5 units. Available to music majors only. Corequisite(s): MU 2700 .
courses.prerequisites: MU 1730 , MU 1731 , or MU 1811 ; appropriate ensemble; passing entrance requirements for upper division studio; and instructor consent.

courses.title: Studio Percussion
courses.description: Weekly individual instructional lessons. Repertoire and technical studies at a higher level than MU 1740, or MU 1741, selected appropriately for timpani, mallet instruments, or other percussion specialties. Jury examination required. Available to Music majors only. May be taken up to five times for a total of 5 units. Available to music majors only. Corequisite(s): MU 2700 .
courses.prerequisites: MU 1740 , MU 1741 , or MU 1811 ; appropriate ensemble; passing entrance requirements for upper division studio; and instructor consent.

courses.title: Studio Keyboard
courses.description: Weekly individual instructional lessons. Repertoire and technical studies at a higher level than MU 1750, or MU 1751, selected appropriately for piano, organ, or harpsichord. Jury examination required. Available to Music majors only. May be taken up to five times for a total credit of 5 units. Available to music majors only. Corequisite(s): MU 2700 .
courses.prerequisites: MU 1750 , MU 1751 , or MU 1811 ; appropriate ensemble; passing entrance requirements for upper division studio; and instructor consent.

courses.title: Studio Guitar
courses.description: Weekly individual instructional lessons. Repertoire and technical studies at a higher level of skill and with more repertoire mastered than for MU 1760, or MU 1761. Jury examination required. Available to Music majors only. May be taken up to five times for a total credit of 5 units. Available to Music majors only. Corequisite(s): MU 2700 .
courses.prerequisites: MU 1760 , MU 1761 , or MU 1811 ; appropriate ensemble; passing entrance requirements for upper division studio; and instructor consent.

courses.title: Studio Voice
courses.description: Weekly individual instructional lessons. Repertoire and technical studies at a higher level than MU 1770, or MU 1771. Jury examination required. Available to Music majors only. May be taken up to five times for a total credit of 5 units. Available to music majors only. Corequisite(s): MU 2700 .
courses.prerequisites: MU 1770 , MU 1771 , or MU 1811 ; appropriate ensemble; passing entrance requirements for upper division studio; and instructor consent.

courses.title: Studio Electric Bass
courses.description: Weekly individual instructional lessons. Repertoire and technical studies at a higher level than MU 1780, or MU 1781. Jury examination required. Available to Music majors only. May be taken up to five times for a total credit of 5 units. Available to Music majors only. Corequisite(s): MU 2700 .
courses.prerequisites: MU 1780 , MU 1781 , or MU 1811 ; appropriate ensemble; passing entrance requirements for upper division studio; and instructor consent.

courses.title: Studio Composition
courses.description: The study of music composition in individual weekly lessons requiring writing music for a variety of instruments, ensembles, and media. Jury examination required. Available to music majors only. May be taken up to four times for a total credit of 4 units. Available to music majors only.
courses.prerequisites: Music majors only, lower division instrument or voice requirements, MU 2251 , and instructor consent.
courses.repeat_for_credit: May be taken multiple times Minimum - Maximum Units: Repeatable up to 4 units.

courses.title: Studio Conducting
courses.description: A series of weekly individual instructional lessons in conducting. Jury examination at the end of each semester. Not available to non-majors. May be taken up to four times for a total credit of 4 units. Available to music majors only.
courses.prerequisites: MU 307, MU 3051 , MU 308 or MU 3061 ; lower division instrument or voice requirements; and instructor consent.

courses.title: Performance Studio Upper Division
courses.description: Repertoire and technical studies as appropriate for each individual instrument or voice, and at a higher level than MU 1811. Jury examination required. Repeatable up to 5 units. A series of weekly specialized individual instruction lessons for students enrolled in the Music Performance Option only. May be taken up to five times for a total credit of 5 units. A series of weekly specialized individual instruction lessons for students enrolled in the Music Performance Option only. Corequisite(s): MU 2700 .
courses.repeat_for_credit: May be taken multiple times Minimum - Maximum Units: Repeatable up to 5 units.

courses.title: Creative Project
courses.description: Projects in music creation or production. May be taken up to four times for a total credit of 4 units.
courses.prerequisites: MU 122 or MU 1211 ; and Instructor consent.

courses.title: Junior Recital
courses.description: Public performance of 25-40 minutes by performance majors only on their instrument or voice. Each performance may be done in collaboration with other performance majors in consultation with appropriate studio teachers. Recital to be completed in spring semester of the junior year.

courses.title: Seminar for Music Industry Studies
courses.description: Weekly seminar examining and discussing issues involved with the music and entertainment industries. Topics may also include making presentations, business practices, and research methods. May be taken up to two times for a total credit of 2 units.

courses.title: Music Studies Integration - Service Learning
courses.description: Integration of the creative, performance, technological, educational, and business aspects of music. Semester-long group projects in conjunction with a community partner, resulting in a finished performance or production with a significant service-learning component. Service learning course.
courses.repeat_for_credit: May be taken multiple times Minimum - Maximum Units: May be taken up to two times for a total credit of 2 units.

courses.title: Non-Profit Music
courses.description: Considering Ensembles, orchestras, symphonies, choruses, and opera companies as business operations. Responsibilities of personnel. Financial concerns, grants, and fundraising. Promotion and marketing. Writing-Intensive courses must be passed with a C or higher to count towards the University’s 3-unit Writing Requirement.
courses.prerequisites: MU 1040 , and junior or senior standing.

courses.title: Music Publishing, Copyright, and Licensing
courses.description: Music publishing administration, copyright law, songwriter and publisher contracts, music licensing and clearances. Legal rights and obligations. Discussion of concepts: personal service, exclusivity and conflict of interest, issues of publicity versus privacy, anti-trust, trademark and labor law.

courses.title: Music for Media
courses.description: Study of record companies, radio stations, music in film, television, games, videos, and multimedia. Administrative and creative functions of music synchronization, its roles and influences, use in advertising, and impact on society.

courses.title: Artist Representation, Promotion, and Touring
courses.description: Roles and responsibilities of performing artist representatives. Credibility and image-building. Techniques for self-promotion.

courses.title: Special Study for Upper Division Students
courses.description: Individual or group investigation, research, studies, or surveys of selected problems at advanced level. Proposals to be initiated by student(s) with guidance from faculty. Total credit limited to 6 units, with a maximum of 3 units per semester.
courses.repeat_for_credit: May be taken multiple times only with different topics Minimum - Maximum Units: Total credit limited to 6 units, with a maximum of 3 units per semester.

courses.title: Song Culture for Schools
courses.description: Methods for song leading and strategies for community-building and inclusion of all school constituencies; identifying and developing song resources from around the world. Presentation of singing activities appropriate for various age groups from kindergarten through high school.

courses.title: Arranging for Voices
courses.description: Techniques of arranging as well as modifying existing compositions for various vocal ensembles.

courses.title: Composing for Video Games and Interactive Media
courses.description: Practical experience in composing, recording, editing, and mixing music for film, video games, and other media. Advanced study of virtual instruments, samplers, and sound design.

courses.title: Theory, History, and Design of Musical Instruments
courses.description: [GE 3C] A modern interpretation of organology, or the study and classification of musical instruments. Explore sound production by classifying and analyzing musical instruments. Examine diverse concepts of musical instruments as tools or beings. Required to design and build a prototype of a new instrument or adaptation of an already existing instrument. Writing-Intensive courses must be passed with a C or higher to count towards the University’s 3-unit Writing Requirement.

courses.title: Western Classical Traditions I
courses.description: Examination of the history of European and American classical music styles and their cultural influences prior to 1900. Research, listening.

courses.title: Western Classical Traditions II
courses.description: Examination of the history of European and American classical music styles and their cultural influences from 1900 to the present. Research, listening.

courses.title: Performance Literature
courses.description: Survey of performance literature of a specified genre. Research and presentation of systematically categorized, historic, graded repertoire for works in a specified genre. May be taken up to two times for a total of 4 units.
courses.prerequisites: MU 2221A ; 3 units of lower division studio; and Instructor consent.

courses.title: Beatlemania
courses.description: [GE 3C or 4C] Investigation of the economic and social conditions that allowed the Beatles to become an enduring phenomenon, from their nascent music making in post-WW II Liverpool and the red light district of Hamburg to their eventual influence on music and popular culture worldwide.
courses.prerequisites: Junior or senior standing; and completion of GE Areas 1 and 2, or Areas A and B4 are recommended.

courses.title: Life and Death in the Arts
courses.description: [GE 3C] Examination of aesthetic expressions in music, art, architecture, dance, literature and theater that express common human experiences: birth, daily life, spirituality, love, and bereavement. Consideration of cultural contexts of all works studied. Collection of works that carry personal meaning. Attendance at arts events.
courses.prerequisites: Junior or senior standing; and completion of GE Areas 1 and 2, or Areas A and B4 are recommended.

courses.title: Tracking and Mixing in Music Recording
courses.description: Advanced techniques for recording, editing and mixing music in a professional digital audio workstation environment. Group projects exploring both historic and modern approaches to tracking and mixing. Advanced exploration of microphone and signal processing techniques.

courses.title: Music Mastering, Editing and Delivery
courses.description: Advanced exploration of the principles and practices of music audio mastering. Group projects explore critical listening, noise reduction, continuity, sweetening, gain structure, dynamics processing, psychoacoustics, editing, fades, Fletcher & Munson loudness curves, and other topics related to audio mastering.

courses.title: Live Sound Production
courses.description: Applied technology and processes used for live sound production and recording in musical productions. Review of acoustics. Historical practices in live sound. Signal processing and noise reduction technologies. Application of consoles, monitoring, microphones, cabling, and microphones in live concert settings.

courses.title: Music Industry Studies Internship
courses.description: Selection and completion of an internship in the music industry or in a faculty-approved related field. Fieldwork. Offered as a 1 unit class in both the fall and spring semesters and as a 2 unit class during summer term. Fieldwork, 1-2 units.
courses.prerequisites: Junior or Senior standing; and Instructor consent.
courses.repeat_for_credit: May be taken multiple times Minimum - Maximum Units: May be taken up to a total credit of 4 units.

courses.title: Senior Project Research and Preparation
courses.description: Research, writing, and preparation of a senior project. Creating a long-term research plan with well-defined milestones and deadlines, culminating with a short presentation. Category to be determined by, and work to be accomplished under the supervision of the instructor.

courses.title: Senior Recital Studio
courses.description: Weekly individual instructional lessons. Repertoire and technical studies in preparation for senior recital. Corequisite(s): MU 4621 and MU 2700 .

courses.title: Senior Project
courses.description: Completion of research, writing and presentation of a project, or work experience in music industry or music education. Category to be determined by, and work to be accomplished under the supervision of appropriate faculty member.

courses.title: Senior Recital
courses.description: Completion of a recital. Repertoire to be determined by, and work to be accomplished under the supervision of appropriate faculty member. Corequisite(s): MU 4610 and MU 2700 .

courses.title: Special Topics for Upper Division Students
courses.description: Group study at an advanced level of a selected well-defined topic or area not covered by a regularly offered course.
courses.repeat_for_credit: May be taken multiple times only with different topics Minimum - Maximum Units: Total credit limited to 6 units applicable to a degree, with a maximum of 2 sections per semester.

courses.description: Group study at an advanced level of a selected well-defined topic or area not covered by a regularly offered course.
courses.repeat_for_credit: May be taken multiple times only with different topics Minimum - Maximum Units: Total credit limited to 6 units applicable to a degree, with a maximum of 2 sections per semester.

courses.description: Group study at an advanced level of a selected well-defined topic or area not covered by a regularly offered course.
